name: Beginner Iron Farm
steps: Choose a location away from other village-related setups and prepare a safe build area.
Build the villager sleeping area and place the required beds.
Move the villagers into their intended positions and make sure they can interact with the required village components.
Build the iron-golem spawning platform and collection area.
Place water so spawned golems are moved toward the collection area.
Set up the hopper and chest collection system.
If the selected design uses a hostile mob to control villager behavior, secure it so villagers cannot be harmed.
Test the farm and check where golems spawn.
Verify that drops reach the hoppers and chest.
mechanics: Iron farms depend on villager and iron-golem spawning mechanics. Exact requirements vary by edition and design.
rate: Varies by design and conditions; do not assume a universal hourly rate.
troubleshooting: No golems: verify the villagers, beds, and required village conditions for the exact design.
Golems outside the farm: inspect nearby valid spawning surfaces.
No item collection: check water flow, hopper orientation, and chest connections.
Low output: make sure the farm remains loaded and nearby mechanics are not interfering.

name: Beginner Creeper Farm
steps: Choose a location suitable for the selected design and prepare the collection area.
Build the lower collection chamber with chests and hoppers.
Build the spawning platforms using the dimensions specified by the source design.
Place trapdoors and other blocks used to control mob spawning.
Add the water channels or flushing mechanism used by the design.
Build the drop or kill area and connect it to the collection system.
Add the required mob-height restrictions exactly as shown in the selected tutorial.
Create a safe AFK position at the distance recommended by the design.
Test the farm and check that creepers reach the collection area.
mechanics: Creeper farms rely on hostile-mob spawning rules and designs that restrict the spawning pool toward creepers. Rates depend on design and spawning conditions.
rate: Highly design-dependent. Do not use another design's advertised rate for this farm.
troubleshooting: Few creepers: check AFK distance and competing mob-spawn locations.
Other mobs spawning: verify the design's carpet/trapdoor/light arrangement.
Creepers not reaching collection: check water channels and drop geometry.
Low rates: reduce competing spawn spaces where the design recommends it.

name: Automatic Sugar Cane Farm
steps: Choose a flat location close enough to remain loaded while you use the farm.
Create a row or platform containing water and the blocks on which sugar cane can be planted.
Plant sugar cane beside the water.
Place pistons so they can break the upper growth.
Place observers to detect growth if using an observer-based automatic design.
Connect observers to the pistons with redstone.
Build the collection area using water, hoppers, or another collection method.
Test the redstone circuit and confirm that growing sugar cane is harvested automatically.
Keep the farm inside loaded chunks when you need it to operate.
mechanics: Sugar cane grows under its normal growth conditions. Automatic designs detect growth and break the upper portion so the lower plant remains.
rate: Depends on farm size, random growth, and whether the area stays loaded.
troubleshooting: Sugar cane not growing: verify the planting block and adjacent water.
Pistons not firing: check observer orientation and redstone connections.
Items missing: check collection water and hopper/chest connections.
Farm stops while away: make sure relevant chunks remain loaded.

steps: Choose a safe Nether location appropriate for the design.
Prepare the portal and collection area according to the selected tutorial.
Build the spawning platforms using the specified blocks and dimensions.
Install the turtle egg and trapdoor arrangement used by the design.
Build the drop and collection system with hoppers and chests.
Complete the surrounding glass or spawning-control structure.
Create the AFK position specified by the tutorial.
Test spawning and item collection.
Use the exact dimensions and material counts from the linked tutorial for the full build.
mechanics: The referenced Java design uses zombified piglin spawning and movement toward a turtle egg, followed by collection and killing for gold-related drops.
rate: The linked tutorial advertises approximately 26 gold blocks per hour for its design; actual rates depend on conditions.
troubleshooting: Low spawning: verify AFK position and spawning conditions.
Mobs not moving: check turtle egg and trapdoor arrangement.
Drops not collected: inspect hopper orientation and chest connections.
Unsafe construction: build and test sections carefully in the Nether.
